# Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics — facts

> Source-anchored units about Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics: 14 across 5 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-29 · 14 units · 5 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] MongoDB documents sessionCatalogPartitions as new in 9.0.1 for mongod; partitioning targets session-catalog lock contention when many sessions are present. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md · keywords: Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/9.0.md
- [statement] Distinguish partition-mutex contention from session-checkout serialization. OperationContextSession may wait because only one user can check out a session at a time; increasing partitions does not remove that exclusivity. SERVER-37499 describes a historical same-session exchange deadlock and explicitly says the scenario had not been observed. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/session/session_catalog.h · keywords: Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-37499
- [statement] SERVER-66960 records a historical optimization that avoids re-locking the session catalog when refreshing the highest child txnNumber, by caching it on the participant session. Its listed fixes are 6.0.0-rc9 and 6.1.0-rc0; it is separate from the later partition-count parameter. (low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-66960 · keywords: Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] SERVER-37499 is a potential-deadlock analysis, not an observed incident: the authors explicitly say they had not observed the scenario. It affects 4.1.3 and lists fix version 4.1.7, so it cannot establish a current 9.0 partitioning defect. (low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-37499 · keywords: Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] MongoDB explicitly recommends retaining the default sessionCatalogPartitions value. The example mongod --setParameter sessionCatalogPartitions=16 illustrates syntax rather than a workload-specific tuning recommendation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md · keywords: Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics
- [statement] Tallent, Mellor-Crummey and Porterfield show why attributing lock-wait idleness only to waiting call paths can be uninformative. Their proposed method uses lock-associated data to attribute spinning-thread idleness to the lock holder and its calling context. They evaluate MADNESS, UTS and SSCA#2 rather than MongoDB. (low confidence) — https://www.cs.rice.edu/~johnmc/papers/hpctoolkit-ppopp-2010.pdf · keywords: Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The default value 0 selects twice the CPU cores available to mongod, capped at 64 partitions. A positive explicit value supplies the partition count directly; 64 is the automatic-selection cap, not a documented cap on explicit settings. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md · keywords: Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/session/session_catalog.cpp
- [statement] MongoDB recommends keeping the default. sessionCatalogPartitions is startup-only, so the documented example mongod --setParameter sessionCatalogPartitions=16 is a startup configuration example, not a runtime tuning instruction. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md · keywords: Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics
- [statement] The master-branch SessionCatalog implementation assigns sessions by the parent logical-session ID hash. Each partition owns a session map and mutex; parent and child sessions remain in one partition. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/session/session_catalog.h · keywords: Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics
- [statement] sessionCatalogPartitions is startup-only. The inspected implementation constructs the partition vector once and never resizes it, so the parameter is not a runtime contention-control knob. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md · keywords: Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/session/session_catalog.h
- [statement] The inspected master constructor registers partition mutexes under sessionCatalogMutex with partition_N labels. Combined with the documented serverStatus lockContentionMetrics interface, this supports checking that tag on a build containing this instrumentation; it does not establish availability in every release. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/session/session_catalog.cpp · keywords: Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md
- [statement] serverStatus excludes lockContentionMetrics by default. Request db.runCommand({serverStatus:1,lockContentionMetrics:1}) for aggregate tags or {serverStatus:1,lockContentionMetrics:{listAll:1}} for individual mutexes. total counts acquisitions, contentions counts acquisitions that waited, and waitCycles measures waiting in CPU cycles, not microseconds. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md · keywords: Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics
- [statement] logicalSessionRecordCache.sessionCatalogSize reports catalog population, including cached transaction or retryable-write state on mongod. It is not a direct measure of mutex contention or of simultaneously executing requests; correlate population with contention counters and operation latency. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md · keywords: Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics
- [statement] For blocked-thread investigation, off-CPU stack analysis complements CPU profiling, which misses time asleep waiting for locks. Off-CPU duration can also include scheduler delay after wakeup, and tracing overhead can alter the workload. This is general diagnostic methodology, not proof of a MongoDB session-catalog bottleneck. (low confidence) — https://www.brendangregg.com/offcpuanalysis.html · keywords: Session catalog partitioning and contention diagnostics
